tasks.gr11-ml-perimeter-area-t3: Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy Term 3 — Measurement: Perimeter, Area and Volume. Ask learners to calculate perimeter of composite 2D shapes, area of rectangles, triangles, circles and composite shapes, surface area of rectangular prisms and cylinders, and volume of prisms and cylinders. Use practical contexts such as tiling a floor, painting a room, filling a container or wrapping a gift box. Ensure consistent use of units (cm², m², cm³, litres).
tasks.gr11-ml-maps-models-t3: Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy Term 3 — Maps, Plans and Models. Ask learners to interpret floor plans and building drawings (top view, front view, side view), identify which view is shown, use annotations and dimensions from a plan to answer applied questions, understand how scale models relate to real objects, and calculate real dimensions from a scaled drawing. Use house plans, room layouts and simple 3D models in South African construction contexts.
tasks.gr11-ml-taxation-t3: Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy Term 3 — Finance: Taxation. Ask learners to calculate VAT at 15% (adding and removing VAT), read and interpret a salary advice slip including gross salary, PAYE, UIF (1%), medical aid deductions and net pay, use a simplified SARS tax table to determine income tax liability, distinguish between tax-inclusive and tax-exclusive prices, and understand the difference between direct and indirect taxes. Use South African SARS and payslip contexts.
tasks.gr11-ml-probability-t3: Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy Term 3 — Probability. Ask learners to list the sample space for simple experiments (coins, dice, spinners, cards), calculate the probability of a single event as a fraction, decimal and percentage, compare relative likelihoods and explain which outcome is more or less likely, interpret probability statements in everyday contexts such as weather forecasts or medical risks, and distinguish between theoretical and experimental probability.
